analysis:
Examined ClusterControlLeadership.swift head text (1-898). The only changes visible are the new optional ClusterControlRequest.stopsBefore field (head 828-836), ClusterControlReply.stopsAsked (869-871), and the ClusterOnboardingLeaderStatus(reply:) initializer (874-878). These fields carry a stop counter over the pairing-keyed link control channel (S07), so a stale start forwarded from a member does not override a later stop. stopsBefore=nil preserves the old serve behavior, and older leaders ignore the field. No authorization, attestation, encryption or key handling changed here. Leadership claim, lease, derivation and solo-admission logic appear unchanged per the complete range map.

The ClusterOnboardingFlow.swift unit (835f62aa717dc58f:0) supplied only metadata, with no text. Its patch excerpt is truncated. It shows new closures, stopsAsked and serveUnlessStopped (head 1518-1525), and provision(stopsBefore:nil) at head 2852. The range map lists many other changed ranges (2901-3539) that I could not inspect, so this is a coverage limit.

Integration must verify the following:
(1) serveUnlessStopped checks stopsAsked under the same lock that stop takes, so the race cannot undo a stop.
(2) A peer-supplied stopsBefore, which is attacker-influenced if the paired Mac is adversarial, cannot cause a serve when stops have been asked. A large or negative value should be compared safely, and its only effect should be refusing to serve, which is benign availability (A-018).
(3) The stopsAsked reply value is used only for display and comparison on the forwarding Mac.

Paired Macs typically share an owner, and requests stay within the pairing-keyed channel. No threat-model entry covers cluster control directly; TB-014 and T-062 are adjacent (cluster gpu-limit). I identified no regression in the visible source.
